about:
California Fine Wire Co. was founded in June 1961 in Grover Beach, California, when Michael A. Greenelsh started the business with a single wire drawing machine. Over six decades, the company has grown into a multi‑million‑dollar operation supplying specialty wire and ribbon worldwide.

The company manufactures and processes fine and ultra‑fine wire in round and flat profiles, with diameters ranging from 0.0004″ to 0.125″. Core processes include precision drawing, enamel coating (insulating), PTFE and ceramic coating, electroplating, flat‑ribbon rolling, annealing, stranding and twisting, cutting, straightening, and spooling. CFW operates 25 enamel coating machines and maintains an in‑house testing laboratory capable of dimensional measurements to 0.00001″ resolution.

CFW serves highly regulated markets including medical, aerospace, defense, electronics, semiconductor, industrial, and research sectors. Its products are used in implanted cardiac devices, drift chambers, semiconductor interconnects, wire‑bonding assemblies, medical devices, aerospace systems, and high‑temperature industrial sensors. The company works with a broad alloy palette—aluminum, copper, gold, nickel, platinum, refractory metals, stainless steel, thermocouple alloys, and composite‑clad conductors.

Founder Michael A. Greenelsh once said the company’s real specialty is fulfilling customers’ specific needs, a philosophy that has guided CFW for over 60 years. The firm emphasizes tight tolerances, traceable raw materials from approved vendors, and a quality system certified to ISO 9001 with ITAR registration for defense work.
